  PROBLEM: An unverifiable tick at the MAX_JUDGE_REPLAY cap produces effective_action=escalate_human. `invoke_stall_judge` then posts the stall-judge comment ("**Decision (effective):** escalate_human", line 22818) and sends the Telegram line "judged=escalate_human, effective=escalate_human" (line 22832) before dispatch. execute_stall_recovery_action then holds the dispatch with "STALL_SKIP issue=N reason=active_set_unverifiable ... action=escalate_human" (line 20414), so no ai:needs-human label and no CRITICAL escalation notice are sent.
  WHY: On the exact tick this PR exists to protect, the issue thread and Telegram tell the operator that the judge escalated to a human when nothing was escalated, and the only trace of the hold is a STALL_SKIP line in the poll log. The source rated this SEVERITY: NIT, mapped here to low. No other reviewer flagged it: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly verified the hold path as correct.

- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh | invoke_stall_judge, lines 22772-22778 (the unverifiable branch and the verified branch)
  PROBLEM: Both branches carry the same three lines that read, validate and increment `.judge_escalate_streak[$n]`. If one copy is edited later and the other is not, the backstop on held ticks will quietly stop matching the backstop on verified ticks.
  FIX: Do the read, validate and increment once inside `if [ "${judge_action}" = "escalate_human" ]`, and keep the state-file write in a nested `if [ "${STALL_ACTIVE_SET_UNVERIFIABLE:-false}" != "true" ]` (est. 8 lines).
- HARDENING: tests/test_orchestrate_stall_active_runs_cache.py | _run_judge_streak_block, right after `block = text[start:end]`
  PROBLEM: The block is cut out by string anchors. If the anchors drift, the test fails with an unclear bash error rather than a clear assertion.
  FIX: `assert block.count("local _judge_escalate_streak=0") == 1 and "effective_action=" in block, block` (est. 1 line).
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  PROBLEM: An unverifiable tick at the MAX_JUDGE_REPLAY cap produces effective_action=escalate_human. The stall-judge comment ("**Decision (effective):** escalate_human", line 22818) and the Telegram line "judged=escalate_human, effective=escalate_human" (line 22832) are posted before dispatch. execute_stall_recovery_action then holds the dispatch with "STALL_SKIP issue=N reason=active_set_unverifiable ... action=escalate_human" (line 20414), with no ai:needs-human label and no CRITICAL escalation notice.

Before this last run, the same tick normalized the verdict to the ladder action. Minimal fix: append "(held: active_set_unverifiable)" to the comment and Telegram line, or emit the STALL_SKIP line before the comment.

  FIX: After slicing, assert that the slice contains "local effective_action" and "normalize_stall_recovery_action" and exactly one "local _judge_escalate_streak=0" (est. 1 line).
